title: Consumer Sector Update for 01/08/2018: CROX,SSI,DRI,WHR,HON,AAPL
text:
CVS -1% 
KO -0.09% 
Consumer stocks were mostly higher Monday, with shares of consumer staples companies in the S&P 500 climbing about 0.1% in afternoon trading while shares of consumer discretionary firms in the S&P 500 were adding almost 0.5% in value. 
In industry news: 
+ Whirlpool ( WHR ) was fractionally higher Monday after the appliance manufacturer said it will be collaborating with Honeywell ( HON ) and Apple ( AAPL ) to develop a line of "smart" appliances linked to Honeywell's connected thermostats and allowing consumers to use their iWatches, iPhones and other Apple devices to remotely manage those products as well as adjusting home temperatures. The companies are expecting to introduce more than 20 of the connected Whirlpool appliances during 2018, they said. 
Among consumer stocks moving on news: 
+ Crocs ( CROX ) raced to a 28-month high on Monday, climbing almost 11% to reach its best price since August 2015 at $13.55 a share, after the shoe company updated its outlook for its Q4 and FY17 ending Dec. 31 ahead of an upcoming appearance at the ICR Capital investor conference starting Tuesday in Orlando, Fla. The company now is projecting Q4 net sales in a range of $195 million to $198 million, up from its prior guidance expecting between $180 million to $190 million and exceeding the Capital IQ consensus call by at least $8.3 million. It also continues to see its FY17 slipping from year-ago levels in the low-single digits, suggesting a range between $1.004 billion to $1.026 billion based on its 1.036 billion in FY16 sales. The Street is at $1.01 billion, representing a 2.4% year-over-year decline. 
In other sector news: 
+ Stage Stores ( SSI ) advanced Monday after the retailer narrowed its projected FY17 net loss to a new range of $0.90 to $1.15 per share after reporting a 1.1% increase in comparable-store sales during the nine weeks ended Dec. 30. The company previously was expecting as large as a $1.25 per share net loss. 
+ Darden Restaurants (DRI) was rising after the restaurant chain raised its FY18 non-GAAP profit outlook to a new range of $4.70 to $4.78 per share compared with its prior view expecting between $4.45 to $4.53 per share.
